requirement: Each listed reference identifies a visible file. Follow `next` to retrieve further pages.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.list_sources.behavior`. I did not request any implementation source.

The requirement has two obligations: (1) each listed reference identifies a visible file, and (2) following `next` retrieves further pages.

**Obligation 1: each reference identifies a visible file**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[listing_continuations_return_complete_paths_from_the_original_listing]` creates 2000 files and an `empty_directory`. After collecting every page, it asserts the references equal exactly the interned `item{i}.rs#` file nodes. So the references identify the expected files, and the directory is not listed.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` covers what "visible" means for `Sources::list`. It runs with and without a git repository and checks the following:
  - Ignored files are excluded, even when Git tracks them.
  - Files in an ignored directory are excluded, even when a nested `.gitignore` re-includes them.
  - `.git` contents are excluded.
  - Nested exceptions and dotfiles are included.
  - `SourceScope::all()` and the default scope give the same listing.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agent_uses_domain_source_tools_in_independent_executions]` is an end-to-end check through the real `list_sources` tool. The test directory has an ignored file and a sibling directory with a similar name. Every entry in the tool output is a numeric node ID. The `selected.txt` index taken from `Sources::list` resolves to the right file when passed to `read_node`. That implies the tool's listing matches the visible-file listing. It runs twice, in independent executions.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_tools_forward_arguments_and_present_discovery_and_read_results]` checks the tool output shape `{"files":[resource]}`. It does this with and without a prefix, and checks that the prefix reaches the provider.

**Obligation 2: following `next`**
- The 2000-file test asserts `next` is present on the first page. It then follows `get_next_page` until `next` is absent. It asserts the concatenation equals the full expected ordered list. A file added after the first call is not in the result, so continuations come from the original listing. Each page delivery has no dependencies.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads]` also follows `next` for `list_sources` and asserts no read registration.

No uncovered condition or boundary the text names, and no gap in assertions, remains.
